memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Of all the creatures living in the water of the seas and the streams you may eat any that have fins and scales. But all creatures in the seas or streams that do not have fins and scales — whether among all the swarming things or among all the other living creatures in the water — you are to regard as unclean. And since you are to regard them as unclean, you must not eat their meat; you must regard their carcasses as unclean. Anything living in the water that does not have fins and scales is to be regarded as unclean by you." - Lev 11:9-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Four verses, and the point is repeated four times: fins and scales, or unclean. God is not being wordy for the sake of it. He is being unmistakably clear, so that no Israelite could later plead confusion.

Notice a small but telling phrase: "you are to regard them as unclean." The uncleanness was not a quality bubbling inside the fish. God declared it, and Israel was to receive that declaration. Their job was not to evaluate whether God's category made sense to them. Their job was to agree with God.

That is a lesson we still need. Much of our struggle with obedience is really a struggle over authority — quietly asking, does this seem reasonable to me? We want to be persuaded before we submit. But faith often means saying, "Lord, You have spoken, and I will regard it as You do," before we understand.

There is a deep grace here too. If God declares something unclean, He can also declare something clean — and that is exactly what He has done with us. In Christ, God has looked at sinners stained by sin and declared them righteous (Rom 8:33-34). Our standing does not rest on our self-assessment. It rests on His word about us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are there areas where you obey God only after being convinced it makes sense?
2. What does it mean for you to "regard" something as God regards it?
3. Do you accept God's declaration over your life in Christ, or your own verdict about yourself?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, teach me to trust Your word above my own reasoning. And thank You that in Christ You have declared me clean — help me to live in the joy of that verdict. Amen.
